thread:
marco: Heads-up — saw a KV slab reshuffle on gpu-az2 during an analytics longctx burst. Memory creep ~3.2GB over ~90s, eviction churn spiked ~8x. Putting profiling snippet below.
emily: Can you paste the pprof snippet and which tenants were hot?

marco: sure, small excerpt from heap profile (truncated):
```
heap/summary: total 12.1GB
kv/pages: 6.4GB (resident 5.8GB)
slab/migrate: 1.9GB (migrated 420k pages)
pagewalk/count: 12.3k (avg cost 320us)
hot-tenant: tenant-analytics-42 -> residency +65% in 60s
```

priya: That pattern screams partial refcounts + fragmentation. Longctx writes keep old KV references alive while many small recency hits bounce pages between slabs. We saw similar behavior in the feb load test but with smaller amplitude.

jin: Were tenant quotas in effect? I remember the tenant had a soft-burst allowance last week. If soft-quota allows spikes, it explains the sudden residency takeover.

emily: pid + config on the node? Could we try smoothing the burst allowance instead of immediate reclaim? In an earlier micro-experiment switching to a 30s smoothing window cut eviction churn ~45% on canary.

marco: node config: gpu-az2-17, kv.surge_smoothing=0 (default), kv.soft_quota=enabled (burst 60s). Example change we tested: 
```yaml
# staging patch
kv.surge_smoothing.window_ms: 30000
kv.surge_smoothing.decay_factor: 0.7
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary deploy -> staging with kv.surge_smoothing=30s at 2089007790 :rocket:

priya: I think we should avoid immediate hard-eviction handoffs — they cause cross-tenant slab migrations. Proposal: probabilistic cooldown sampling + decay of burst credit. Also consider light-weight per-tenant slab pinning for active longctx sessions to reduce migrations.

marco: +1. I'll draft an RFC for tenant-scaled cooldown + migration avoidance heuristics. Happy to prototype a pinning latch that prevents moving a slab for X seconds after longctx activation. :memo:

jin: If we add cooldown, ensure we have a safety path: if node free mem < critical watermark then fallback to aggressive reclaim (hard-evict). We don't want an OOM cascade.

emily: I'll schedule a focused staging test: longctx length=512, burst mix (analytics heavy + low-reuse tenants) tomorrow morning. Will capture metrics: residency bounce, pagewalks/token, slab-migrations/s. Ping me when RFC lands and I'll run the experiment.

marco: Great. Next steps: 1) I open RFC (tenant-cooldown-and-pinning) 2) priya prototypes sampling cooldown logic 3) emily runs staging load test with smoothing enabled 4) jin adds the memory-watermark fallback to reclaimer. Tagging @priya @jin @emily for visibility.

marco: TL;DR: short-term: enable kv.surge_smoothing=30s on canary nodes; mid-term: tenant-scaled cooldown + optional per-tenant slab pin; must keep hard-evict fallback behind memory watermark.

emily: sounds good. :thumbsup:
